definitions.explanation: Thin, noodle-like strips of konjac (konnyaku), a gelatinous food made from the konjac plant. Commonly used in hot pot dishes and simmered dishes.

examples.japanese: すき{焼|や}きに{糸|いと}こんにゃくを{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Put shredded konjac into the sukiyaki.

examples.japanese: {糸|いと}こんにゃくは{低|てい}カロリーでダイエットに{向|む}いている。
examples.english: Konjac noodles are low in calories and good for dieting.

examples.japanese: {肉|にく}じゃがを{作|つく}るとき、{糸|いと}こんにゃくを{入|い}れると{食|た}べ{応|ごた}えが{出|で}る。
examples.english: When making nikujaga, adding konjac noodles gives the dish more substance.

notes:
USAGE:
{糸|いと}こんにゃく is a staple ingredient in Japanese home cooking, especially in simmered dishes ({煮物|にもの}) and hot pot dishes ({鍋|なべ}). The name literally means "thread konjac" because of its thin, string-like shape.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {糸|いと}こんにゃくを{入|い}れる (add konjac noodles)
- {糸|いと}こんにゃくの{下|した}ゆで (parboiling konjac noodles)
- {糸|いと}こんにゃくの{炒|いた}め{煮|に} (stir-fried and simmered konjac noodles)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {糸|いと}こんにゃく: thin noodle-shaped konjac
- しらたき: similar thin konjac noodles (more common in eastern Japan)
- {板|いた}こんにゃく: block konjac (slab form)
